root_cause.text: The `adxl380_irq_handler` function failed to validate that the FIFO entry count reported by the hardware status registers was a multiple of the enabled scan element count (`st->fifo_set_size`) before reading data in batches, allowing the loop to access memory beyond the actual available data.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds `fifo_entries = rounddown(fifo_entries, st->fifo_set_size);` immediately before the read loop in `adxl380_irq_handler`, directly addressing the CVE description which states that the sensor fills the FIFO one sample at a time while the handler assumes complete batches of N samples.

intent_record.intent_summary: Rounds down FIFO entry count to set size to ensure safe processing of complete data blocks.
intent_record.what: Inserted a line calling rounddown() to align fifo_entries to st->fifo_set_size before the processing loop.
intent_record.how: Ensures the loop only processes complete FIFO data sets by truncating any partial remainder, preventing potential buffer overruns or invalid reads.

grouping_result.intent: Rounds down FIFO entry count to set size to ensure safe processing of complete data blocks.

relevance_review.reason: The vulnerability arises from processing incomplete FIFO blocks which causes out-of-bounds memory access. Rounding down the entry count to the nearest multiple of the set size ensures only complete, valid blocks are processed, directly addressing the missing validation described in the root cause.
